claims: Theorem A: For the same adapted input class and same horizon, a strongly causal zero-preserving closed loop with mean-square gain G2 has literal gain G1 <= sqrt(2) G2; source-checked monotone Lenglart application, not equality of gamma levels.

Theorem B: On the infinite horizon only, a fixed deterministic stationary linear finite-window preview controller of the specified K/tap/kernel form has G2/sqrt(3) <= G1 <= sqrt(2)G2. The lower bound uses signed independent input blocks, exact superposition under one Brownian path, no physical reset, and an in-text finite-n truncation/Chebyshev bound.

Corollary C: Scalar fixed state feedback with c != 0 and nonzero output d has finite infinite-horizon literal gain iff q = 2a_closed + sigma_closed^2 < 0. For q >= 0, each Gamma is defeated by a deterministic compactly supported pulse train, with quantified choices of L,M,delta,n. This is not a prescribed-gamma general synthesis solution.

Direct sufficient synthesis corollary: a strict quadratic storage block inequality for u=Kx gives internal mean-square stability and literal gain <= sqrt(2)g for any fixed delay h. It is conservative and derives directly from Ito, not an unverified Riccati import.

Mean-square gain comparison lower bound is infinite-horizon only and retains arbitrary adapted Brownian-functional disturbances.
Scalar q=0 boundary diverges linearly in block length in equation25; deterministic pulse train is finite energy for every chosen n and L.
